content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/.claude/skills/zimmerMANNReview

Review of a colleague's work. Same architecture as the build chain — ground truth, a gated audit,
then present and stop — tailored to a PR you did not write.

**Intended model: Sonnet 5 at maximum effort.**

**The thing that makes it work:** you hold the ground truth and the adjudication, and delegate only
the reading. Reviewers are cheap and fallible; measurements are expensive and authoritative. Keep
those on opposite sides of the line.

**Input:** `PR #84` — a PR number.

**Scale to the work.** A two-file PR does not get four reviewers. Nothing too crazy, no
overthinking.

---

## Phase 1 — ground truth. Yours, not an agent's.

### Frame the PR

Base SHA, head SHA, files changed, ±lines. **Use the live head** — a stale ref has already caused a
whole round of re-verification here.

### Requirements — Jira, Confluence, Figma

Build the same requirements picture a PreBuild would build, then judge the PR against it. Every
scope argument, every "this is missing", every "this wasn't asked for" gets decided against these
words — not the PR description's paraphrase of them.

**Jira.** Pull the full ticket: description, ACs, linked work items, and — critically — the full
comment thread. Decisions made in comments routinely contradict the description and never make it
back into the ACs. Flag: untestable ACs · requirements that contradict each other or the comments
· a linked blocker still open · a decision in comments that the implementation may not have seen ·
**evidence that a different PR, branch, or assignee is already working the same ticket.**

**Anything flagged here goes in your next status update to Marcel, even when it's correctly out
of scope for the PR itself.** "Not my concern for this review" and "not worth telling him" are
different judgements — a discovery can be exactly right to leave alone in the diff and still be
something he needs to know exists. Deciding not to act on it is not the same as deciding not to
mention it.

**Confluence.** If the ticket links a PRD, TSD, or integration doc, read it. The Jira ACs are
often a summary; the full requirements live in Confluence. Flag: a Confluence requirement not
reflected in the ACs · a doc that contradicts the ticket · a doc that describes an approach the
PR does not follow.

**Figma.** Read the design systematically — not just the node cited in the PR description.

- **All variants and states:** hover, focus, active, disabled, loading, error, empty, selected.
  A state the PR doesn't implement is a finding; a state Figma doesn't specify is an open
  question to name, not a reason to skip. **Before concluding a state is simply absent from a
  component, check whether an adjacent or parent element carries that same signal instead** (the
  button not the swatch, the row not the cell) — a concern can be fully handled by the design and
  still look like a gap if you only look at the one element it doesn't live on.
- **Annotations:** interaction notes and spacing/token callouts often hold the real spec detail.
- **Currency:** is the linked node archived or superseded? An archived node that still renders
  is a trap — triage before judging.
- **Tokenisation:** does every colour, spacing, and type value map to an existing `--zimm-*`
  token, or did the author introduce a new one? A new token is Tier 1; confirm it was handled
  correctly.
- **Measurement:** FRAMES and INSTANCES report real boxes (comparable to CSS). TEXT nodes report
  cap-height (not comparable). Never file a mismatch from a TEXT node. Never cross-compare the
  Design System file and the Designs file — they are different sources.

**If the Jira-linked nodes are incomplete, partial, or outdated — stop and ask Marcel for the
correct nodes before continuing.** One node URL per variant and per state, not one per component.
Do not guess at a neighbouring node that looks close, do not proceed on a partial picture, and do
not treat an archived node as the spec. The whole review hangs on having the right design source;
a wrong node produces false findings and misses real ones. This is the one step where asking
beats estimating.

The visual checklist in Phase 2 tells you what to verify in the browser. This step tells you
**what to look for** — you cannot run that checklist without knowing what the design intended.

### The rubric

`.claude/rules/*`, `AGENTS.md`, and the exemplar PR the work should follow. These are what the PR
is judged against — a reviewer applying general best practice instead of house rules generates
noise that reads like signal.

**If the PR edits the rule files it would be judged against, read the rubric at the BASE commit.**
Judging a PR against its own edited rules is circular. Rule-file edits are reviewed separately, as
changes.

### Run the gates yourself — on head and on base

```
npx tsc --noEmit
npm run test
npm run lint
node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs
```

Then run them again at the base SHA. **Without a baseline you cannot tell a failure the PR
introduced from one it inherited**, and inherited debt reported as a new violation is the fastest
way to lose a reviewer's trust.

Three false signals, all seen on this repo:

1. **Non-zero at a healthy baseline.** `lint` and `audit:tokens` both exit non-zero on a clean
   tree. Compare counts; ignore exit codes.
2. **A pass having run nothing.** `vitest.config.ts` sets `passWithNoTests: true` — a typo'd path
   filter exits 0 having run zero tests. **Assert on the reported item count, never the exit code.**
3. **A skipped required check looks green.** `detect-changes` can skip `unit-tests` and
   `storybook-test` entirely, and the PR still shows mergeable. Report which checks actually
   *executed* versus which were skipped. A skip proves nothing.

### CodeRabbit is an input, not a verdict

If CodeRabbit has reviewed, read it — then verify it. It has run as low as 1-in-6 correct on this
repo. Its findings enter Phase 2 as claims to test, exactly like anyone else's.

---

## Phase 2 — audit

### Fan out

`zm-tester` dispatches reviewers on **distinct but overlapping** briefs. The overlap is the
mechanism: two agents converging independently is your confidence signal; two disagreeing is where
you learn something.

Give each: the diff, the ticket verbatim, and **your measured gate numbers — then forbid them from
re-running the gates.** Their budget goes on what the gates cannot see.

Angles that have earned their place: correctness and regression · conventions, structure and tier
ownership · contract fidelity, if the PR ports, wraps or overrides something · failure modes and
security · token and styling strategy (bandaid tokens, missing semantic tokens, state
exhaustiveness).

**Design fidelity is yours, not an agent's.** Agents have no browser and no Figma access — ask
them to reason from code and they will, but they cannot see what renders. For any PR that changes
rendered output, run this checklist yourself at the PR's head:

| What to check | How |
|---|---|
| Dimensions and spacing match Figma frames | DevTools computed, vs. Figma inspect |
| Colours resolve to the correct semantic token | DevTools → Computed → colour value |
| Typography uses `textStyle=`, not raw `fontSize` | DevTools → font-size is a `var()` |
| All designed states render correctly (hover, focus, active, disabled) | Tab through + `:hov` in DevTools |
| Responsive behaviour matches the spec | Resize or toggle responsive mode |
| No visual regressions on adjacent components | Scroll the surrounding page |

If a state is not in the PR's recipe at all, no agent will flag it — only you will notice. The
visual checkpoint is the only gate on design fidelity.

**When the PR has a live MRT preview URL, use browser automation — not just your own browser.**
Navigate to the preview URL with Chrome browser tools, screenshot each component across the full
responsive range — not just canonical endpoint widths, but at each design breakpoint and its
boundaries (just above and just below where the layout shifts). Inspect computed styles via
element selectors rather than guessing from code. This produces a concrete, shareable record
(screenshots, exact computed values) rather than impressions, and it runs the same check Marcel
would run himself — so discrepancies surface before comments are drafted, not after.

**Then walk visual and browser-verified findings through one at a time with Marcel before
finalizing them.** Present the screenshot or computed value, let him reproduce or contradict it
from his own browser. This is the step that catches tool artifacts (Popper-positioned layers a
screenshot mechanism misses, click simulations that differ from real interactions, a transition
that hasn't settled when the measurement ran) before they become posted comments. A finding Marcel
has personally verified is a finding you can post with confidence. One that he contradicts is a
finding you drop and learn from — that counts as the verification step working, not failing.

Use **fresh contexts, not forks.** A fork inherits your assumptions about what "done" looks like,
which is exactly what you want tested.

### Scope

`zm-orchestrator` returns the scope verdict — does this PR deliver its ticket, neither under nor
over. Both directions carry equal weight.

### Verify the findings before they reach you

`zm-scorer`, briefed in **findings mode** — it is not scoring the PR, it is scoring the claims:

> For each finding: does it survive scrutiny? Reproduce it or say you could not. Return
> **CONFIRMED** (reproduced from source), **PLAUSIBLE** (consistent with what you read, decisive
> evidence missing — say exactly what would settle it), or **UNSUPPORTED** (the citation does not
> support the claim; say what is actually true). Where a finding's conclusion is broader than its
> search supports, downgrade it — that is the single most common failure mode. Any "X exists
> nowhere" claim must state its search scope in the same sentence.

Expect roughly a third to be wrong. You should not be adjudicating unverified claims.

**This applies to your own findings too, not just an agent's.** Anything you notice directly
while gathering ground truth (a comparison against a related PR, a claim sitting in a code
comment, an assumption about what a value implies) gets the same CONFIRMED/PLAUSIBLE/UNSUPPORTED
discipline before it is presented as fact — a finding is not exempt from scrutiny just because no
agent produced it. Route it through the same questions: what is the search scope, does one
uncorroborated source actually settle this, and has a stated number been measured or only assumed.

**A claim about how a bug resolves needs the same reproduction as the bug itself.** Verification
effort naturally goes toward proving the failure happens, not toward proving what you claim happens
next — "self-heals on the next hover," "clears on reload," "only affects this one instance." These
read as a supporting detail inside a bigger writeup, not as their own finding, so they skip the
CONFIRMED/PLAUSIBLE discipline above by default. If you didn't reproduce the recovery, mark it
PLAUSIBLE and say so, exactly like any other unconfirmed claim.

### Classify every survivor

- **In-scope defect** — belongs to this PR. Only these can become comments.
- **Out-of-scope** — real, but not this PR's problem. Name the owning ticket or the person.
- **Nitpick** — cosmetic, brings no value. Recorded, never posted.

A true finding raised on the wrong PR is still noise.

---

## Phase 3 — adjudicate

### Present, in "ELI5 but I'm the FED Lead" register

1. **Gate table** — head versus base, with which checks actually executed
2. **Findings, ranked by what it costs to ignore** — not by severity label, by consequence.
   Each with `file:line`, CONFIRMED or PLAUSIBLE, and its classification
3. **The scope verdict**
4. **What nobody verified** — the honest section, and what stops a clean result reading as proof
5. **Your adjudications to make**, one at a time via AskUserQuestion

### The verdict is yours

**Approve or request changes is your call, and so is every disputed finding.** The agents produce
findings; you decide what they mean. Where two reviewers disagree, go to source yourself — do not
average them, and do not take the more confident one. Confidence and correctness are not correlated
in agent output.

Name one premise every reviewer agreed on, and make someone attack it.

### Then the comments

Draft general and inline comments for the in-scope defects only. Structure that has worked:

- Verdict up front
- The small cleanups separated from the one thing that genuinely needs the author's call
- A blocker framed as **a question about intent**, citing the project's own doc by section
- The two acceptable resolutions named
- Where an independent tool corroborated, say so

**Natural human language without sacrificing the technical accuracy.** No em-dashes. No Claude or
CodeRabbit attribution. No citation of any local-only doc — cite `AGENTS.md` or `.claude/rules/*`
instead, which the author can actually open. No opening praise or thanks before the substance — a
review comment states findings, it does not warm up first. Watch for jargon-stacking too: a
sentence naming three technical concepts back to back reads like documentation, not like one
person explaining something to another — split it or say it plainer instead.

**Never reveal that a parallel or competing implementation of the same ticket exists**, even in
passing ("the other version of this feature," "the other build") — a review comment is visible to
the whole team, and disclosing a second, independent attempt at the same story is not this
reviewer's call to make. When a content rule like this applies, sweep every drafted comment for
it before presenting the batch, not just the one currently under discussion — a rule caught on
one comment and missed on a near-identical one is a leak, not a style nit.

**Nothing posts until you say so.** Show the full set, post the batch on your go.

---

## The loop

The author pushes changes. Re-review.

**Scoped by default:** which findings the new commits resolved, which they missed, and whether the
fixes introduced anything new. Settled items are not re-litigated.

**Full pass when the diff has genuinely moved** — a substantial new commit, or a change to the
approach rather than the details. **Say which one you ran.**

Repeat until approved. Confirm your own requested changes actually landed rather than taking
"done" on trust.

---

## Ownership and phrasing — every outward-facing surface

Every finding names **who resolves it**: the author, Tim, a designer, a BA, QA.

**Where the owner is senior or lateral, phrase it as a question — never a directive.** "Should this
route via X, or have I misread it?" not "change this to X." Ask confirmatorily.

Before posting, count the asks. A review that mentions one person eight times reads as hiding
behind their authority.

**Be scrupulously fair to the author.** Separate "broke a documented rule" from "hit a gap the
process never covered", and where the process failed them, say so. Flag explicitly any finding
where the fact is true but the characterisation is unfair — better to drop a finding than post an
unfair one.

---

## Hard rules

- **Never write code.** This skill reviews. If a fix is needed on your own branch, that is Build.
- **Never post a comment, a review, or a verdict without an explicit go.**
- **Never resolve a thread you did not open.**
- **Never report inherited debt as a new violation.** Baseline first.
- **Never flag out-of-scope findings onto the PR.** Record them for yourself.
- **Say what you could not verify.** A review that finds nothing has not been shown to be capable
  of finding anything.

addedLines: - agent-sdk-dev:agent-sdk-verifier-py: Use this agent to verify that a Python Agent SDK application is properly configured, follows SDK best practices and documentation recommendations, and is ready for deployment or testing. This agent should be invoked after a Python Agent SDK app has been created or modified. (Tools: All tools)

- agent-sdk-dev:agent-sdk-verifier-ts: Use this agent to verify that a TypeScript Agent SDK application is properly configured, follows SDK best practices and documentation recommendations, and is ready for deployment or testing. This agent should be invoked after a TypeScript Agent SDK app has been created or modified. (Tools: All tools)
- claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`; (5) `claude plugin eval` (writing and running plugin eval suites, its JSON/report, sandbox, CI, early-access enablement) and the `/skill-doctor` report. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- code-simplifier:code-simplifier: Simplifies and refines code for clarity, consistency, and maintainability while preserving all functionality. Focuses on recently modified code unless instructed otherwise. (Tools: All tools)

- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- feature-dev:code-architect: Designs feature architectures by analyzing existing codebase patterns and conventions, then providing comprehensive implementation blueprints with specific files to create/modify, component designs, data flows, and build sequences (Tools: Glob, Grep, LS, Read, NotebookRead, WebFetch, TodoWrite, WebSearch, KillShell, BashOutput)

- feature-dev:code-explorer: Deeply analyzes existing codebase features by tracing execution paths, mapping architecture layers, understanding patterns and abstractions, and documenting dependencies to inform new development (Tools: Glob, Grep, LS, Read, NotebookRead, WebFetch, TodoWrite, WebSearch, KillShell, BashOutput)

- feature-dev:code-reviewer: Reviews code for bugs, logic errors, security vulnerabilities, code quality issues, and adherence to project conventions, using confidence-based filtering to report only high-priority issues that truly matter (Tools: Glob, Grep, LS, Read, NotebookRead, WebFetch, TodoWrite, WebSearch, KillShell, BashOutput)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- plugin-dev:agent-creator: Use this agent when the user asks to "create an agent", "generate an agent", "build a new agent", "make me an agent that...", or describes agent functionality they need. Trigger when user wants to create autonomous agents for plugins. Examples:

<example>
Context: User wants to create a code review agent
user: "Create an agent that reviews code for quality issues"
assistant: "I'll use the agent-creator agent to generate the agent configuration."
<commentary>
User requesting new agent creation, trigger agent-creator to generate it.
</commentary>
</example>

<example>
Context: User describes needed functionality
user: "I need an agent that generates unit tests for my code"
assistant: "I'll use the agent-creator agent to create a test generation agent."
<commentary>
User describes agent need, trigger agent-creator to build it.
</commentary>
</example>

<example>
Context: User wants to add agent to plugin
user: "Add an agent to my plugin that validates configurations"
assistant: "I'll use the agent-creator agent to generate a configuration validator agent."
<commentary>
Plugin development with agent addition, trigger agent-creator.
</commentary>
</example> (Tools: Write, Read)

- plugin-dev:plugin-validator: Use this agent when the user asks to "validate my plugin", "check plugin structure", "verify plugin is correct", "validate plugin.json", "check plugin files", or mentions plugin validation. Also trigger proactively after user creates or modifies plugin components. Examples:

<example>
Context: User finished creating a new plugin
user: "I've created my first plugin with commands and hooks"
assistant: "Great! Let me validate the plugin structure."
<commentary>
Plugin created, proactively validate to catch issues early.
</commentary>
assistant: "I'll use the plugin-validator agent to check the plugin."
</example>

<example>
Context: User explicitly requests validation
user: "Validate my plugin before I publish it"
assistant: "I'll use the plugin-validator agent to perform comprehensive validation."
<commentary>
Explicit validation request triggers the agent.
</commentary>
</example>

<example>
Context: User modified plugin.json
user: "I've updated the plugin manifest"
assistant: "Let me validate the changes."
<commentary>
Manifest modified, validate to ensure correctness.
</commentary>
assistant: "I'll use the plugin-validator agent to check the manifest."
</example> (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- plugin-dev:skill-reviewer: Use this agent when the user has created or modified a skill and needs quality review, asks to "review my skill", "check skill quality", "improve skill description", or wants to ensure skill follows best practices. Trigger proactively after skill creation. Examples:

<example>
Context: User just created a new skill
user: "I've created a PDF processing skill"
assistant: "Great! Let me review the skill quality."
<commentary>
Skill created, proactively trigger skill-reviewer to ensure it follows best practices.
</commentary>
assistant: "I'll use the skill-reviewer agent to review the skill."
</example>

<example>
Context: User requests skill review
user: "Review my skill and tell me how to improve it"
assistant: "I'll use the skill-reviewer agent to analyze the skill quality."
<commentary>
Explicit skill review request triggers the agent.
</commentary>
</example>

<example>
Context: User modified skill description
user: "I updated the skill description, does it look good?"
assistant: "I'll use the skill-reviewer agent to review the changes."
<commentary>
Skill description modified, review for triggering effectiveness.
</commentary>
</example> (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob)

- pr-review-toolkit:code-reviewer: Use this agent when you need to review code for adherence to project guidelines, style guides, and best practices. This agent should be used proactively after writing or modifying code, especially before committing changes or creating pull requests. It will check for style violations, potential issues, and ensure code follows the established patterns in CLAUDE.md. Also the agent needs to know which files to focus on for the review. In most cases this will be recently completed work which is unstaged in git (can be retrieved by running git diff). However there can be cases where this is different, make sure to specify this as the agent input when calling the agent. Typical triggers include the user asking for a review of a feature they just implemented, the assistant proactively reviewing its own newly-written code before declaring a task done, and a final pre-PR check before opening a pull request. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:code-simplifier: Use this agent when code has been written or modified and needs to be simplified for clarity, consistency, and maintainability while preserving all functionality. This agent should be triggered automatically after completing a coding task or writing a logical chunk of code. It simplifies code by following project best practices while retaining all functionality. The agent focuses only on recently modified code unless instructed otherwise.

Examples:

<example>
Context: The assistant has just implemented a new feature that adds user authentication to an API endpoint.
user: "Please add authentication to the /api/users endpoint"
assistant: "I've implemented the authentication for the /api/users endpoint. Here's the code:"
<function call omitted for brevity>
<commentary>
Since a logical chunk of code has been written (authentication feature), use the Task tool to launch the code-simplifier agent to improve the code's clarity and maintainability while preserving functionality.
</commentary>
assistant: "Now let me use the code-simplifier agent to refine this implementation for better clarity and maintainability"
</example>

<example>
Context: The assistant has just fixed a bug by adding several conditional checks.
user: "Fix the null pointer exception in the data processor"
assistant: "I've added the necessary null checks to prevent the exception:"
<function call omitted for brevity>
<commentary>
After modifying code to fix a bug, use the code-simplifier agent to ensure the fix follows best practices and maintains code quality.
</commentary>
assistant: "Let me refine this bug fix using the code-simplifier agent to ensure it follows our best practices"
</example>

<example>
Context: The assistant has just refactored a function to improve performance.
user: "Optimize the data sorting algorithm for better performance"
assistant: "I've optimized the sorting algorithm. Here's the updated implementation:"
<function call omitted for brevity>
<commentary>
After completing a performance optimization task, use the code-simplifier agent to ensure the optimized code is also clear and maintainable.
</commentary>
assistant: "Now I'll use the code-simplifier agent to ensure the optimized code is also clear and follows our coding standards"
</example> (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:comment-analyzer: Use this agent when you need to analyze code comments for accuracy, completeness, and long-term maintainability. This includes (1) after generating large documentation comments or docstrings, (2) before finalizing a pull request that adds or modifies comments, (3) when reviewing existing comments for potential technical debt or comment rot, and (4) when you need to verify that comments accurately reflect the code they describe. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:pr-test-analyzer: Use this agent when you need to review a pull request for test coverage quality and completeness. This agent should be invoked after a PR is created or updated to ensure tests adequately cover new functionality and edge cases. Typical triggers include the user asking whether tests on a freshly-created PR are thorough, an updated PR adding new logic that needs coverage analysis, and a final pre-merge double-check before marking a PR ready. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:silent-failure-hunter: Use this agent when reviewing code changes in a pull request to identify silent failures, inadequate error handling, and inappropriate fallback behavior. This agent should be invoked proactively after completing a logical chunk of work that involves error handling, catch blocks, fallback logic, or any code that could potentially suppress errors. Examples:

<example>
Context: Daisy has just finished implementing a new feature that fetches data from an API with fallback behavior.
Daisy: "I've added error handling to the API client. Can you review it?"
Assistant: "Let me use the silent-failure-hunter agent to thoroughly examine the error handling in your changes."
<Task tool invocation to launch silent-failure-hunter agent>
</example>

<example>
Context: Daisy has created a PR with changes that include try-catch blocks.
Daisy: "Please review PR #1234"
Assistant: "I'll use the silent-failure-hunter agent to check for any silent failures or inadequate error handling in this PR."
<Task tool invocation to launch silent-failure-hunter agent>
</example>

<example>
Context: Daisy has just refactored error handling code.
Daisy: "I've updated the error handling in the authentication module"
Assistant: "Let me proactively use the silent-failure-hunter agent to ensure the error handling changes don't introduce silent failures."
<Task tool invocation to launch silent-failure-hunter agent>
</example> (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:type-design-analyzer: Use this agent when you need expert analysis of type design in your codebase. Specifically use it (1) when introducing a new type to ensure it follows best practices for encapsulation and invariant expression, (2) during pull request creation to review all types being added, and (3) when refactoring existing types to improve their design quality. The agent will provide both qualitative feedback and quantitative ratings on encapsulation, invariant expression, usefulness, and enforcement. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

- vercel:ai-architect: Specializes in architecting AI-powered applications on Vercel — choosing between AI SDK patterns, configuring providers, building agents, setting up durable workflows, and integrating MCP servers. Use when designing AI features, building chatbots, or creating agentic applications. (Tools: All tools)

- vercel:deployment-expert: Specializes in Vercel deployment strategies, CI/CD pipelines, preview URLs, production promotions, rollbacks, environment variables, and domain configuration. Use when troubleshooting deployments, setting up CI/CD, or optimizing the deploy pipeline. (Tools: All tools)

- vercel:performance-optimizer: Specializes in optimizing Vercel application performance — Core Web Vitals, rendering strategies, caching, image optimization, font loading, edge computing, and bundle size. Use when investigating slow pages, improving Lighthouse scores, or optimizing loading performance. (Tools: All tools)

- zm-implementer: Executes one step of a Zimmermann PWA Kit build plan. Use when a planned step needs to be implemented in code. Writes only the files the step names, and stops rather than expanding scope. (Tools: Read, Write, Edit, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- zm-orchestrator: Scope and spec-conformance checker for an in-flight Zimmermann build. Use after an implementation step to judge whether the work delivers exactly what the plan specified — neither less nor more. Reports a verdict; never edits code. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- zm-planner: Synthesises gathered evidence into an executable build plan for a Zimmermann PWA Kit story. Use after all sources have been gathered, when the findings need to become a sequenced plan with per-step pass criteria. Does not gather evidence itself and does not write code. # Sprint Scope

*Draft (2026-06-23). To be refined as sprints are confirmed.*

Defines the dependency order of the build. Claude reads this to understand what code exists at
each stage. **When working in a sprint, do not reference code, components, hooks, or
integrations from a later sprint — they do not exist yet.**

Contentful works/integration will be done as part of each corresponding functional story.

For *what is currently done vs pending* within the active sprint, see
[projectState.md](./projectState.md). This file is the dependency map; `projectState.md`
is the live progress tracker.

---

## Current position

**Sprint 0 — Foundation (in progress).**
See [projectState.md](./projectState.md) for the live breakdown.

---

## Sprint 1 — 29 Jun – 10 Jul

**Squad A (FED):**
- Common UI Components
- Homepage & Navigation (Part 1)
- Regional Storefront (Part 1)

**Squad B (FED):**
*Not started yet* 

---

## Sprint 2 — 13 Jul – 24 Jul

**Depends on:** Sprint 1 complete

**Squad A (FED):**
- Homepage & Navigation (Part 2)
- Regional Storefront (Part 2)
- PDP (Part 1)
- PLP (Part 1)

**Squad B (FED):**
*Not started yet*

---

## Sprint 3 — 27 Jul – 7 Aug

**Depends on:** Sprint 2 complete

**Squad A (FED):**
- PDP (Part 2)
- PLP (Part 2)
- Cart

**Squad B (FED):**
- Search & Recommendations

---

## Sprint 4 — 10 Aug – 21 Aug

**Depends on:** Sprint 3 complete

**Squad A (FED):**
- Checkout Flow & Delivery (excl. custom payments that will be done in Sprint 6)

**Squad B (FED):**
- Promotions

---

## Sprint 5 — 24 Aug – 4 Sep

**Depends on:** Sprint 4 complete

**Squad A (FED):**
- Order Management

**Squad B (FED):**
- Store Locator
- Zimmerse

---

## Sprint 6 — 7 Sep – 11 Sep

**Depends on:** Sprint 5 complete

**Squad A (FED):**
- Payments (Adyen, etc)
- Credit Notes & Gift Cards (GiveX)

**Squad B (FED):**
- Zimmerse

---

## Sprint 7

**Depends on:** Sprint 6 complete

**Squad A (FED):**
- Returns & Refunds

**Squad B (FED):**
- SEO & Analytics (GTM, Optimizely, Crazy Egg, Inside Chat, etc)

---

## How Claude uses this file

When implementing a feature, Claude checks which sprint it belongs to and does not reference
components, hooks, or integrations from later sprints.

If a task requires something from a later sprint, Claude stops and asks:
> "This feature depends on [X] which is Sprint [N] work. Should I build a placeholder, or is
> Sprint [N] already complete?"

Reference this file in prompts when sprint context matters:
> "We are currently in Sprint 1. Build the global header skeleton. Do not wire up basket
> state — that is Sprint 3."

1	# Project State
2	
3	*Current status of all services, integrations, deploy status, what's complete, and what's pending. Update this file at the start of each session if anything has changed.*
4	
5	*Last updated: 2026-08-24 (SFCC-55 global footer — decomposed into `ui-kits/` atoms/molecules/organisms with co-located `<name>.css.ts` recipes; wired to live Contentful `footerConfig` with region-aware resolution; `useUiCopy` promoted to an app-wide Context; `var(--zimm-*)` now required over bare Chakra token keys; `scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs` added. See In Progress). Previous: 2026-08-18 (zimmTokens.ts made fully derived from the other `foundation/*` files instead of hand-retyped literals; `zimmButton.css.ts` established as the single source of truth for button styling, `globalStyles.ts`'s conflicting `.zimm-btn-*` class system removed; `spacing.ts`/`typography.ts` converted px → rem for WCAG 1.4.4; `header.ts`/`listMenu.ts` brought onto the same `var(--zimm-*)` token convention; new `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md` documents the resulting styling-source hierarchy. See What's Complete). Previous: 2026-07-16 (PR #30 and PR #35 merged — e2e-localhost fixed and re-enabled, root cause was a swallowed click failure in `BasePage.js`'s consent handling; `deploy-test.yml` added for the previously undeployable `test` tier; README command reference added; Stage/UAT promotion order reconciled across docs; a tag-based environment-promotion proposal is drafted on Confluence, not yet implemented — see What's Pending). Previous sweep 2026-06-25 against updated Zimmermann Functional Requirements.xlsx via /update-prds-from-xlsx — CFD-067 Company Name + VAT/Tax ID optional fields confirmed for EU/UK checkout; PRC-03 future-dated markdown with timezone mapping confirmed; PRC-07 tax class via AP21 taxonomy ID + Avalara/Global-e coverage confirmed; PRC-13 catalogue markdowns + promotions in order payload confirmed; PRC-46 coupon handling at Global-e challenged and kept Open; HPC-018 header icon set resolved — Search/Account/Bag only, Locate Boutique/Contact Us/Newsletter confirmed not in header; SPR-03 editorial paragraph confirmed not collapsible, read-more action only); trimmed stale entries.*
6	
7	## Phase
8	**Detailed Design** — Some functional requirements have been confirmed (30 Apr 2026 sign-off); others are still open. No production build has started beyond scaffolding.
9	
10	Workshop sign-off tracker: All workshops signed off (2026-04-30 through 2026-06-24). Row-level opens tracked under Unresolved Dependencies below.
11	
12	*For system roles and integration details, see [architecture.md](architecture.md). Open items that block implementation are listed under "Unresolved Dependencies" below.*
13	
14	## Integrations
15	| System | Status | Notes |
16	|---|---|---|
17	| Salesforce Commerce Cloud (SFCC) | Mock | Sandbox; not yet Zimmermann's production org |
18	| Contentful | Mock | Demo space; not yet Zimmermann's production space |
19	| Global-e | Not started | Pricing via SFCC price books (AP21 base RRP + fixed pricelists, nightly FX job — PRC-34..55, now Confirmed 2026-06-01). Global-e handles shipping/duties/taxes at international checkout via vendor cartridge + iframe injection. REG-040 struck (superseded by REG-041, confirmed). |
20	| Didomi | Not started | |
21	| Omneo | Not started | |
22	| Emarsys | Not started | |
23	| MuleSoft | Not started | |
24	| NewStore OMS | Not started | SIT parallel CI lane scaffolded 2026-05-20: `.github/workflows/digital-sit.yml` + [05.6 - Environment Details](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/285540356) (Confluence). Six-tier topology reference at [Environment Topology & Promotion Path](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/304840708) (Confluence). Pending: SFCC SIT credentials, `MRT_SIT_URL` / `MRT_TEST_URL` GitHub Secrets, `push:sit` / `activate:sit` npm scripts, `mobify.config.js` `sit` env entry, `config/sit.js`. |
25	| AP21 | Not started | |
26	| Adyen | Not started | Apple Pay, Google Pay, Klarna: targeting August 2026 (not launch) |
27	| Narvar | Not started | |
28	| Google Maps API | Not started | Address validation/autocomplete. Now confirmed to also back **address-book** validation (CRM-053) — the same validation used in cart/checkout is reused in the account address book; users may still opt into the full manual form. |
29	| Avalara | Not started | Covers US domestic, NZ, New Caledonia, **and EU domestic** (confirmed 2026-06-19 via Third_Party_Integrations sheet update). UK uses SFCC native VAT tables. |
30	| GiveX | Not started | Gift card processing (physical + digital). Gift Cards workshop targeting sign-off 2026-05-12 |
31	| Inside Chat | Not started | |
32	| Transperfect | Not started | Direct Contentful↔Transperfect workflow confirmed (REG-047 update); SFCC strings via JSON files. PWA only consumes translated payloads |
33	| Google Business API | Not started | Daily store-hours feed into SFCC; PWA renders only (out-of-band) |
34	| Feedonomics | Not started | Product feed for downstream marketing channels (PRD-071); no PWA runtime touchpoint |
35	
36	## What's Complete
37	- PWA Kit scaffolding with TypeScript strict mode (`@salesforce/retail-react-app` bumped from v9.1.1 → v10.0.0 on 2026-05-18)
38	- Overrides pattern established
39	- Country/locale config (`overrides/app/config/countries.ts`)
40	- Contentful Studio integration (pointing to mock account)
41	- **Contentful content model tooling** (`npm run sync:contentful` / `npm run install:contentful`) — authors `scripts/contentful/content-types/` as one organization-scoped Environment Template and installs it per environment via the Management API (replaced the earlier per-environment sync.js + migrations pipeline, 2026-08-23).
42	- **ShoppableImage component decommissioned** (2026-08-23) — it was a Studio Experience component + standard content type synced 2026-05-11, but had 0 entries and was removed (content type, React component, and its hotspotMarker/hotspotPopup sub-components) once the region/link/footerConfig content model landed. `CollectionHero` and `ImageText` are the remaining Studio Experience components.
43	- Basic SFCC Commerce SDK integration (pointing to mock account)
44	- Home page / home-preview page merged
45	- Functional requirements signed off (Checkout, Returns, Orders, Payments, Cart, Regional, Content, PDP/PLP, Search, CRM)
46	- Design token foundation ported from the F2R Handover into `overrides/app/theme/foundation/` (`colour.ts`, `typography.ts`, `gridSystem.ts`, `spacing.ts`, `sizes.ts`, `motion.ts`, `zimmTokens.ts`) plus the `.zimm-*` global classes in `overrides/app/theme/globalStyles.ts`; composed in `overrides/app/theme/index.ts`, per-component overrides now co-located beside their component as `<name>.css.ts` and registered in `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts` (`theme/components/` itself now holds only `header.ts`/`listMenu.ts` as registered recipes, plus `navConstants.ts` and `footerShared.ts` for values shared across split-out files). Delivered as a foundation for the manual UI build (branch `feature/design-tokens-implementation-to-dev`); F2R component work continues separately on `feature/f2r-component-registry` and `feature/f2r-implementation-workflow`. Futura Round **is** self-hosted as of SFCC-55 — two faces (400/500) ship from `overrides/app/static/fonts/` and are served on every tier. Open with the UI designer: primary-action hover contrast (2.96:1), inverse focus ring, and button-height / nav letter-spacing deviations from the Handover.
47	- **Token architecture hardened** (2026-08-18): `zimmTokens.ts` (the `--zimm-*` CSS-var registry) is now fully derived from the other `foundation/*` files via imports instead of hand-duplicated literals, closing the drift risk the original port above carried. `typography.ts` gained a proper `fontSizes`/`lineHeights`/`letterSpacings`/`fontWeights` scale layer. `spacing.ts`/`typography.ts` converted px → rem (WCAG 1.4.4); within those two files, px is kept only for hairline geometry (border widths, focus-ring offsets — now named tokens in `spacing.ts`'s `focusRingOffsets`). `zimmButton.css.ts`'s provisional height/padding constants are a separate, already-flagged px exception (not hairline geometry) — see below. `zimmButton.css.ts` is now the single source of truth for button styling — `globalStyles.ts`'s conflicting `.zimm-btn-*`/`.zimm-text-btn-*` classes (different heights, transparent-vs-opaque secondary background, zero interactive states) were removed entirely; any button must use Chakra's `<Button>`, never a class. `header.ts`/`listMenu.ts` brought onto the same `var(--zimm-*)` convention (no direct `foundation/` imports, no Chakra semantic colour-token names). New `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md` documents the styling-source hierarchy, unit rules, the alias-is-a-reference-not-a-copy principle, and a real gotcha: importing an already-overridden component via the SFCC base path resolves correctly in the real app but silently renders the unstyled base version in Storybook/Vitest (the `ccExtensibility` resolver is webpack-only, neither tool loads it). Still open, flagged inline rather than silently resolved: `zimmButton.css.ts`'s `BTN_HEIGHT_LG`/`BTN_HEIGHT_SM` (50px/41px prototype values) disagree with the Handover-sourced `actionSizes.height.lg`/`.md` (52px/40px); `BTN_PADDING_Y` (5px) has no Handover token at all — both pending UI-designer sign-off.
48	- **Header override** (`overrides/app/components/header/index.tsx`): two-row layout, brand logo via `BrandLogo` component (overrides base SVG at `overrides/app/assets/svg/brand-logo.svg`), uppercase nav with `::after` hover animation, Account/Saved/Bag text buttons with matching animation, chevrons hidden. Still being refined visually against Figma.

    2. **Primary enforcement — one GitHub Ruleset covers both naming and immutability:** Settings → Rules → Rulesets → New tag ruleset, targeting `v*`, with a "tag name pattern" rule requiring `^v\d+\.\d+\.\d+(-rc\.\d+|-hotfix\.\d+)?$` plus "restrict creation," "restrict updates," and "restrict deletion" all enabled. This genuinely hard-blocks a non-matching tag at push time *and* prevents force-push/delete on matching tags — all on GitHub.com, not Enterprise Server-only (corrected from an earlier draft of this note, which wrongly split this into a separate "tag protection rules" step and claimed pattern-blocking wasn't possible on GitHub.com). Keep a `push: tags: ['*']` validation workflow too, as defense-in-depth / for a clearer failure message than the raw ruleset rejection gives.
    3. A version-guard step added to each `deploy-*.yml` (test/sit/stg/uat/prod) — fetch the environment's current deployed tag via `gh api repos/ZimmermannAU/zimmermann-pwa/deployments?environment=<env>`, semver-compare against the tag being deployed (use the `semver` npm package, not hand-rolled bash comparison — pre-release identifiers must be dot-separated, e.g. `-rc.10` vs `-rc.2`, or numeric comparison breaks), fail on a downgrade. **`<env>` must be the actual GitHub Environment name, not the workflow-file suffix** — they diverge for `stg` (`deploy-stg.yml` targets the `staging` Environment, not `stg`; we hit this exact mismatch once already this session, commit `12bf91b`). Map each tier explicitly (`stg` → `staging`, everything else matches its filename) rather than deriving it from the filename. Fail closed if the environment name is wrong or the API call errors — a genuine first-ever deployment (no prior Deployment record at all) is fine to proceed, but an unresolvable environment/API error is not the same thing and must not be treated as "nothing to compare against, allow it."
    4. **A Test-tier CI gate** — new, decided 2026-07-16. Proposed shape (not yet confirmed, see the page's remaining two open questions): a second job appended to `deploy-test.yml` that runs a P0-only Playwright suite against whatever was just deployed, so the run's pass/fail becomes the "safe to promote to SIT" signal — deliberately deploy-then-gate rather than SIT Gate's gate-then-deploy, since `Test` is on-demand (`workflow_dispatch`, including raw feature branches) and has no push/PR event to hang a pre-check on.
    5. Wire `/generate-changelog`'s existing `gh release create` offer into the "cut the final tag" step — no new tooling, the skill already does this.
  - **Governance — needs squad-lead + Integration-lead review before merging:**
    6. A new `.claude/rules/tagging.md` (or fold into `.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md`, already auto-loaded on `release/*`/`hotfix/*`) documenting the tag convention and instructing Claude to always use `npm version`, never hand-construct a tag string.
    7. `AGENTS.md`'s branch table / the Confluence Branching Guide itself, once the team has actually reviewed and approved the proposal — this repo's `AGENTS.md` requires both squad leads and the Integration lead to sign off on changes to itself, stronger than the usual verified-session Tier 1 exception.

39	
40	// Local Project Components
41	import AboveHeader from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/_app/partials/above-header'

47	import OfflineBanner from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/offline-banner'
48	import OfflineBoundary from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/offline-boundary'
49	import {HideOnDesktop, HideOnMobile} from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/responsive'
50	import ScrollToTop from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/scroll-to-top'

52	import CheckoutFooter from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/pages/checkout/partials/checkout-footer'
53	import CheckoutHeader from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/pages/checkout/partials/checkout-header'
54	
55	// Hooks
56	import {AddToCartModalProvider} from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-add-to-cart-modal'
57	import {AuthModal, useAuthModal} from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-auth-modal'
58	import {BonusProductSelectionModalProvider} from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-bonus-product-selection-modal'
59	import {useCurrentBasket} from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-current-basket'
60	import {useCurrentCustomer} from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-current-customer'
61	import {
62	    DntNotification,
63	    useDntNotification
64	} from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-dnt-notification'
65	import useMultiSite from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-multi-site'
66	import {useStoreLocatorModal} from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-store-locator'
67	import {useUpdateShopperContext} from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-update-shopper-context'
68	
69	// HOCs
70	import {withCommerceSdkReact} from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/with-commerce-sdk-react/with-commerce-sdk-react'
71	
72	import {PageDesignerProvider} from '@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react/page-designer'
73	import PageDesignerInit from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/page-designer-init'
74	
75	// Localization
76	import {IntlProvider} from 'react-intl'
77	
78	// Others
79	import {
80	    CAT_MENU_DEFAULT_NAV_SSR_DEPTH,
81	    CAT_MENU_DEFAULT_ROOT_CATEGORY,
82	    DEFAULT_LOCALE,
83	    DEFAULT_SITE_TITLE,
84	    HOME_HREF,
85	    STORE_LOCATOR_IS_ENABLED,
86	    THEME_COLOR
87	} from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/constants'
88	import {fetchTranslations, getTargetLocale} from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/locale'
89	import {flatten, isServer, watchOnlineStatus} from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/utils'
90	
91	import Seo from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/seo'
92	import ShopperAgent from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/shopper-agent'
93	import {initializeRegistry} from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/page-designer/registry'
94	
95	// Initialize registry synchronously at module load time so components are available during SSR
96	initializeRegistry()
97	import {getCommerceAgentConfig} from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/config-utils'
98	import {getPathWithLocale} from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/url'
99	import {useShopperAgent} from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-shopper-agent'
100	
101	const PlaceholderComponent = () => (
102	    <Center p="2">
103	        <Spinner size="lg" />
104	    </Center>
105	)
106	
107	const DrawerMenuItemWithData = withCommerceSdkReact(
108	    ({itemComponent: ItemComponent, data, ...rest}) => (
109	        <Fade in={true}>
110	            <ItemComponent {...rest} item={data} itemComponent={DrawerMenuItemWithData} />
111	        </Fade>
112	    ),
113	    {
114	        hook: useCategory,
115	        queryOptions: ({item}) => ({
116	            parameters: {
117	                id: item.id
118	            }
119	        }),
120	        placeholder: PlaceholderComponent
121	    }
122	)
123	
124	const ListMenuContentWithData = withCommerceSdkReact(
125	    ({data, ...rest}) => (
126	        <Fade in={true}>
127	            <ListMenuContent {...rest} item={data} />
128	        </Fade>
129	    ),
130	    {
131	        hook: useCategory,
132	        queryOptions: ({item}) => ({
133	            parameters: {
134	                id: item.id,
135	                levels: 2
136	            }
137	        }),
138	        placeholder: PlaceholderComponent
139	    }
140	)
141	
142	const App = (props) => {
143	    const {children} = props
144	    const {data: categoriesTree} = useCategory({
145	        parameters: {id: CAT_MENU_DEFAULT_ROOT_CATEGORY, levels: CAT_MENU_DEFAULT_NAV_SSR_DEPTH}
146	    })
147	    const categories = flatten(categoriesTree || {}, 'categories')
148	    const {getTokenWhenReady} = useAccessToken()
149	    const {usid} = useUsid()
150	    const appOrigin = useAppOrigin()
151	    const activeData = useActiveData()
152	    const history = useHistory()
153	    const location = useLocation()
154	    const authModal = useAuthModal()
155	    const dntNotification = useDntNotification()
156	    const {site, locale, buildUrl} = useMultiSite()
157	    const {
158	        isOpen: isStoreLocatorOpen,
159	        onOpen: onOpenStoreLocator,
160	        onClose: onCloseStoreLocator
161	    } = useStoreLocatorModal()
162	    const storeLocatorEnabled = getConfig()?.app?.storeLocatorEnabled ?? STORE_LOCATOR_IS_ENABLED
163	    const {req} = useServerContext()
164	
165	    const [isOnline, setIsOnline] = useState(true)
166	    const styles = useStyleConfig('App')
167	    const {isOpen, onOpen, onClose} = useDisclosure()
168	
169	    // Determine Page Designer mode from URL - use req for server-side detection
170	    const pageDesignerMode = useMemo(() => {
171	        const queryParams = location?.search || ''
172	        if (queryParams.includes('mode=EDIT')) return 'EDIT'
173	        else if (queryParams.includes('mode=PREVIEW')) return 'PREVIEW'
174	        return undefined
175	    }, [req?.url])
176	
177	    const targetLocale = getTargetLocale({
178	        getUserPreferredLocales: () => {
179	            // CONFIG: This function should return an array of preferred locales. They can be
180	            // derived from various sources. Below are some examples of those:
181	            //
182	            // - client side: window.navigator.languages
183	            // - the page URL they're on (example.com/en-GB/home)
184	            // - cookie (if their previous preference is saved there)
185	            //
186	            // If this function returns an empty array (e.g. there isn't locale in the page url),
187	            // then the app would use the default locale as the fallback.
188	
189	            // NOTE: Your implementation may differ, this is just what we did.
190	            return [locale?.id || DEFAULT_LOCALE]
191	        },
192	        l10nConfig: site.l10n
193	    })
194	
195	    // If the translation file exists, it'll be served directly from static folder (and won't reach this code here).
196	    // However, if the file is missing, the App would render a 404 page.
197	    const is404ForMissingTranslationFile = /\/static\/translations\/compiled\/[^.]+\.json$/.test(
198	        location?.pathname
199	    )
200	
201	    // Fetch the translation message data using the target locale.
202	    const {data: messages} = useQuery({
203	        queryKey: ['app', 'translations', 'messages', targetLocale],
204	        queryFn: () => {
205	            if (is404ForMissingTranslationFile) {
206	                // Return early to prevent an infinite loop
207	                // Otherwise, it'll continue to fetch the missing translation file again
208	                return {}
209	            }
210	            return fetchTranslations(targetLocale, appOrigin)
211	        },
212	        enabled: isServer
213	    })
214	
215	    // Used to conditionally render header/footer for checkout page
216	    const isCheckout = /\/checkout$/.test(location?.pathname)
217	
218	    const {l10n} = site
219	    // Get the current currency to be used through out the app
220	    const currency = locale.preferredCurrency || l10n.defaultCurrency
221	
222	    // Handle creating a new basket if there isn't one already assigned to the current
223	    // customer.
224	    const {data: customer} = useCurrentCustomer()
225	    const {data: basket, dataUpdatedAt: basketQueryLastUpdateTime} = useCurrentBasket()
226	    const config = getConfig()
227	
228	    const updateBasket = useShopperBasketsMutation('updateBasket')
229	    const updateCustomerForBasket = useShopperBasketsMutation('updateCustomerForBasket')
230	
231	    useEffect(() => {
232	        // update the basket currency if it doesn't match the current locale currency
233	        if (basket?.currency && basket?.currency !== currency) {
234	            updateBasket.mutate({
235	                parameters: {basketId: basket.basketId},
236	                body: {currency}
237	            })
238	        }
239	    }, [basket?.currency])
240	
241	    const commerceAgentConfiguration = useMemo(() => {
242	        return getCommerceAgentConfig()
243	    }, [config.app.commerceAgent])
244	
245	    useEffect(() => {
246	        // update the basket customer email
247	        if (
248	            basket &&
249	            customer?.isRegistered &&
250	            customer?.email &&
251	            customer?.email !== basket?.customerInfo?.email
252	        ) {
253	            updateCustomerForBasket.mutate({
254	                parameters: {basketId: basket.basketId},
255	                body: {
256	                    email: customer.email
257	                }
258	            })
259	        }
260	    }, [customer?.isRegistered, customer?.email, basket?.customerInfo?.email])
261	
262	    useEffect(() => {
263	        // Listen for online status changes.
264	        watchOnlineStatus((isOnline) => {
265	            setIsOnline(isOnline)
266	        })
267	    }, [])
268	
269	    // Handle updating the shopper context
270	    useUpdateShopperContext()
271	
272	    useEffect(() => {
273	        // Lets automatically close the mobile navigation when the
274	        // location path is changed.
275	        onClose()
276	    }, [location])
277	
278	    const onLogoClick = () => {
279	        // Goto the home page.
280	        const path = buildUrl(HOME_HREF)
281	
282	        history.push(path)
283	
284	        // Close the drawer.
285	        onClose()
286	    }
287	
288	    const onCartClick = () => {
289	        const path = buildUrl('/cart')
290	        history.push(path)
291	
292	        // Close the drawer.
293	        onClose()
294	    }
295	
296	    const onAccountClick = () => {
297	        // Link to account page if registered; Header component will show auth modal for guest users
298	        const path = buildUrl('/account')
299	        history.push(path)
300	    }
301	
302	    const onWishlistClick = () => {
303	        // Link to wishlist page if registered; Header component will show auth modal for guest users
304	        const path = buildUrl('/account/wishlist')
305	        history.push(path)
306	    }
307	
308	    const {actions: shopperAgentActions} = useShopperAgent()
309	
310	    const trackPage = () => {
311	        activeData.trackPage(site.id, locale.id, currency)
312	    }
313	
314	    useEffect(() => {
315	        trackPage()
316	    }, [location])
317	
318	    const getHrefForLocale = (localeId) =>
319	        `${appOrigin}${getRouterBasePath()}${getPathWithLocale(localeId, buildUrl, {
320	            location: {...location, search: ''}
321	        })}`
322	
323	    return (
324	        <Box className="sf-app" {...styles.container}>
325	            <StorefrontPreview getToken={getTokenWhenReady} getBasePath={getRouterBasePath}>
326	                <IntlProvider
327	                    onError={(err) => {
328	                        if (!messages) {
329	                            // During the ssr prepass phase the messages object has not loaded, so we can suppress
330	                            // errors during this time.
331	                            return
332	                        }
333	                        if (err.code === 'MISSING_TRANSLATION') {
334	                            // NOTE: Remove the console error for missing translations during development,
335	                            // as we knew translations would be added later.
336	                            logger.warn('Missing translation', {
337	                                namespace: 'App.IntlProvider',
338	                                additionalProperties: {
339	                                    errorMessage: err.message
340	                                }
341	                            })
342	                            return
343	                        }
344	                        throw err
345	                    }}
346	                    locale={targetLocale}
347	                    messages={messages}
348	                    // For react-intl, the _default locale_ refers to the locale that the inline `defaultMessage`s are written for.
349	                    // NOTE: if you update this value, please also update the following npm scripts in `template-retail-react-app/package.json`:
350	                    // - "extract-default-translations"
351	                    // - "compile-translations:pseudo"
352	                    defaultLocale={DEFAULT_LOCALE}
353	                >
354	                    <CurrencyProvider currency={currency}>
355	                        <Seo>
356	                            <meta name="theme-color" content={THEME_COLOR} />
357	                            <meta name="apple-mobile-web-app-title" content={DEFAULT_SITE_TITLE} />
358	                            <link
359	                                rel="apple-touch-icon"
360	                                href={getAssetUrl('static/img/global/apple-touch-icon.png')}
361	                            />
362	                            <link rel="manifest" href={getAssetUrl('static/manifest.json')} />
363	
364	                            {/* Urls for all localized versions of this page (including current page)
365	                            For more details on hrefLang, see https://developers.google.com/search/docs/advanced/crawling/localized-versions */}
366	                            {site.l10n?.supportedLocales.map((locale) => (
367	                                <link
368	                                    rel="alternate"
369	                                    hrefLang={locale.id.toLowerCase()}
370	                                    href={getHrefForLocale(locale.id)}
371	                                    key={locale.id}
372	                                />
373	                            ))}
374	                            {/* A general locale as fallback. For example: "en" if default locale is "en-GB" */}
375	                            <link
376	                                rel="alternate"
377	                                hrefLang={site.l10n.defaultLocale.slice(0, 2)}
378	                                href={getHrefForLocale(locale.id)}
379	                            />
380	                            {/* A wider fallback for user locales that the app does not support */}
381	                            <link rel="alternate" hrefLang="x-default" href={`${appOrigin}/`} />
382	                        </Seo>
383	
384	                        {commerceAgentConfiguration?.enabled === 'true' && (
385	                            <ShopperAgent
386	                                commerceAgentConfiguration={commerceAgentConfiguration}
387	                                basketDoneLoading={basketQueryLastUpdateTime > 0}
388	                            />
389	                        )}
390	
391	                        <ScrollToTop />
392	
393	                        <Box id="app" display="flex" flexDirection="column" flex={1}>
394	                            <SkipNavLink zIndex="skipLink">Skip to Content</SkipNavLink>
395	                            {storeLocatorEnabled && (
396	                                <StoreLocatorModal
397	                                    isOpen={isStoreLocatorOpen}
398	                                    onClose={onCloseStoreLocator}
399	                                />
400	                            )}
401	                            <Island hydrateOn={'visible'}>
402	                                <Box {...styles.headerWrapper}>
403	                                    {!isCheckout ? (
404	                                        <>
405	                                            <AboveHeader />
406	                                            <Header
407	                                                onMenuClick={onOpen}
408	                                                onLogoClick={onLogoClick}
409	                                                onMyCartClick={onCartClick}
410	                                                onMyAccountClick={onAccountClick}
411	                                                onWishlistClick={onWishlistClick}
412	                                                onStoreLocatorClick={onOpenStoreLocator}
413	                                                onAgentClick={shopperAgentActions.open}
414	                                            >
415	                                                <HideOnDesktop>
416	                                                    <DrawerMenu
417	                                                        isOpen={isOpen}
418	                                                        onClose={onClose}
419	                                                        onLogoClick={onLogoClick}
420	                                                        root={
421	                                                            categories?.[
422	                                                                CAT_MENU_DEFAULT_ROOT_CATEGORY
423	                                                            ]
424	                                                        }
425	                                                        itemsKey="categories"
426	                                                        itemsCountKey="onlineSubCategoriesCount"
427	                                                        itemComponent={DrawerMenuItemWithData}
428	                                                    />
429	                                                </HideOnDesktop>
430	
431	                                                <HideOnMobile>
432	                                                    <ListMenu
433	                                                        root={
434	                                                            categories?.[
435	                                                                CAT_MENU_DEFAULT_ROOT_CATEGORY
436	                                                            ]
437	                                                        }
438	                                                        itemsKey="categories"
439	                                                        itemsCountKey="onlineSubCategoriesCount"
440	                                                        contentComponent={ListMenuContentWithData}
441	                                                    />
442	                                                </HideOnMobile>
443	                                            </Header>
444	                                        </>
445	                                    ) : (
446	                                        <CheckoutHeader />
447	                                    )}
448	                                </Box>
449	                            </Island>
450	                            {!isOnline && <OfflineBanner />}
451	                            <AddToCartModalProvider>
452	                                <BonusProductSelectionModalProvider>
453	                                    <SkipNavContent
454	                                        style={{
455	                                            display: 'flex',
456	                                            flexDirection: 'column',
457	                                            flex: 1,
458	                                            outline: 0
459	                                        }}
460	                                    >
461	                                        <Box
462	                                            as="main"
463	                                            id="app-main"
464	                                            role="main"
465	                                            display="flex"
466	                                            flexDirection="column"
467	                                            flex="1"
468	                                        >
469	                                            <OfflineBoundary isOnline={false}>
470	                                                <PageDesignerProvider
471	                                                    clientId="pwa-kit-client"
472	                                                    targetOrigin="*"
473	                                                    usid={usid}
474	                                                    mode={pageDesignerMode}
475	                                                >
476	                                                    <PageDesignerInit />
477	                                                    {children}
478	                                                </PageDesignerProvider>
479	                                            </OfflineBoundary>
480	                                        </Box>
481	                                    </SkipNavContent>
482	
483	                                    <Island hydrateOn={'visible'}>
484	                                        {!isCheckout ? <Footer /> : <CheckoutFooter />}
485	                                    </Island>
486	
487	                                    <AuthModal {...authModal} />
488	                                    <DntNotification {...dntNotification} />
489	                                </BonusProductSelectionModalProvider>
490	                            </AddToCartModalProvider>
491	                        </Box>
492	                    </CurrencyProvider>
493	                </IntlProvider>
494	            </StorefrontPreview>
495	        </Box>
496	    )
497	}
498	
499	App.propTypes = {
500	    children: PropTypes.node
501	}
502	
503	export default App

## What the PR does
Copy-first ports `overrides/app/components/_app/` (a Tier 2 "Global Shell" file per `.claude/rules/protectedFiles.md` — it did not exist as an override before this PR, base SFCC's `_app/index.jsx` was rendering unmodified on every tier) and removes the base template's `DntNotification` placeholder consent modal (Salesforce's own demo scaffolding — literal Lorem-ipsum body copy, no config flag to disable it). It also modifies `vitest.config.ts` (Tier 1 test config) to add two `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` subpath aliases (`/components`, `/page-designer`) ahead of the existing bare-specifier alias, and adds one ambient type declaration (`getRouterBasePath(): string`) to `overrides/app/types/vendor.d.ts`.

## Jira ticket SFCC-863 (verbatim description)
"**Context** Surfaced while investigating SFCC-860's Lighthouse `categories.performance` finding (LCP 6.4s / score 0.1) against a real deployed build. The Largest Contentful Paint element turned out not to be an image — the homepage currently has none — but literal placeholder text inside a modal: 'Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet...'. Traced to `@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-dnt-notification.js`'s `DntNotification` component, rendered unconditionally in the base `_app/index.jsx` — Zimmermann has no override for `_app` yet, so this base behaviour is live as-is on every tier. Salesforce's own source comment confirms it's not meant to ship: `// Placeholder for the consent tracking form for demonstration purposes`. It auto-opens via a `useEffect` whenever `selectedDnt === undefined` (i.e. on every fresh session with no stored preference) — confirmed no config-level toggle exists to suppress it.
**Why this matters beyond performance** Per AGENTS.md's Consent & Marketing section, Didomi is meant to own all consent gating for this project (REG-054, not-yet-started). This base component is not that — real shoppers on any tier without an `_app` override are currently seeing literal 'Lorem ipsum' copy in a tracking-consent dialog.
**Scope**
- Override `overrides/app/components/_app/index.tsx` (Tier 2 — Global Shell, 'Both Squads — coordinate before touching' per protectedFiles.md; copy-first from `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/_app/index.jsx` per AGENTS.md's Copy-first rule) to stop rendering `<DntNotification>`
- Header and Footer are both already overridden — the new `_app` override must import them via relative paths (`../header`, `../footer`), not the base SFCC path, per `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`'s 'Importing an already-overridden component' section, or Storybook/Vitest will silently exercise the unstyled base versions
- Decide how this interacts with the broader Didomi integration (REG-054) — does DNT tracking-consent get replaced by a Didomi-driven flow entirely, or does this story just remove the placeholder and Didomi work supersedes it later?
- Full TypeScript port of `_app` is non-trivial: ~500 lines, many hooks — budget real review time, not a quick patch

- No placeholder/demo consent copy is ever shown to a real shopper on any tier
- Lighthouse's LCP on the homepage reflects real content, not this modal
- Header/Footer overrides continue to render correctly through the new `_app` override (spot-check Storybook and the real app, not just tsc)"

- PR base (`develop` at the PR's merge-base, commit `9ab9aad`): `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-marcel-a-n-navarro-Dev-zimmermann-pwa/315b63a0-b125-4f80-a22b-5eb85ce56fd5/scratchpad/pr84-base`

content.text:
## PR #84 review — findings for adjudication

The PR moved twice during this review (a conflict-resolving merge landed, then CodeRabbit re-reviewed it), so everything below is against the **true current head**, `da8c37036`, re-verified after the move.

### Gate table

| Check | Base (`9ab9aad`) | PR head (`da8c37036`, current) |
|---|---|---|
| `tsc --noEmit` | clean | clean |
| `vitest` | 45 files / 678 tests, all pass | 46 files / 691 tests, all pass |
| `eslint` (changed files) | — | 0 errors / 3 warnings (matches PR's own claim) |
| `audit:tokens` | 1 pre-existing violation (unrelated) | same, not re-run after the merge — flagging as unconfirmed rather than assuming |
| CI: Unit tests (Vitest) | — | ✅ pass |
| CI: Storybook interaction & a11y | — | ❌ **fails** — build succeeds, but the serve step times out waiting for the local server. Looks like CI flake, not a code regression (I couldn't establish a clean base rate to be certain) |
| CI: Playwright/BrowserStack | — | skipped (change-scoped, expected) |
| Git mergeable | CONFLICTING (at time of open) | MERGEABLE (resolved by merge commit) |
| `reviewDecision` | — | **REVIEW_REQUIRED**, `mergeStateStatus: BLOCKED` |

### Findings, ranked by consequence

**1. Zero qualifying human approval exists — this is why the PR is blocked.** `overrides/app/components/_app/` is Tier 2 Global Shell; CODEOWNERS requires approval from squad-a, squad-b, tier-2, or tier-1 approvers — anyone but the author. TimLavelleACC's in-thread reply ("I'm a Tier1 approver... so this is approved") lands as `COMMENTED`, never `APPROVED` — GitHub structurally blocks author self-approval, and Tier-1 status doesn't substitute for the separate Tier-2 gate anyway. You did approve it ("LGTM!"), but GitHub auto-dismissed that the moment the merge commit landed — correctly, since the registry corruption below was introduced *after* your review, not before it.

**2. `.claude/registry/components.md` and `hooks.md` are corrupted on the current head.** The merge-conflict resolution kept both sides instead of regenerating: `App` is now listed twice, once as `Override | ... | 21` consumers and once as `Base | ... | 7` consumers — the registry now contradicts itself on the literal subject of this PR. `useEinstein`/`useToast` similarly duplicated. CodeRabbit's own review on this exact commit flagged this by name as CHANGES_REQUESTED, then **approved the identical commit 16 seconds later with nothing fixed**. Trivial fix: rerun `node scripts/generateRegistry.mjs` and commit. Worth knowing as a concrete data point on CodeRabbit's reliability here, beyond the general track record.

**3. `_app/index.tsx:49` imports `HideOnDesktop`/`HideOnMobile` from the base SFCC path instead of `../responsive`.** This is exactly the mistake the ticket named and the PR correctly avoided for Header/Footer/DrawerMenu/ListMenu — missed for a fifth already-overridden dependency in the same file. `responsive`'s override genuinely changes behavior (768px breakpoint split vs. Chakra's default 992px). Zero production impact (webpack's resolver saves it), but the test's own mock repeats the same wrong path, so nothing currently catches it. One-line fix.

**4. Storybook/a11y CI check currently fails** on the true head (see gate table). Worth a rerun before treating it as settled either way.

**5. Minor: PR body claims "47 files / 682 tests"; actual is 46/691 now (was 46/680 at the commit it describes).** Cosmetic.

**Not findings (checked and cleared):** the disputed "`useAppOrigin` was a default import" claim is unverifiable either direction — no artifact shows an intermediate state — shouldn't be posted as a defect. A pre-existing, byte-identical-to-base `pageDesignerMode` staleness-after-hydration issue exists but is inherited debt, not new. Test-mock fidelity across ~30 mocks was traced to real export shapes and is clean. Token/styling usage is clean. content.text:
Good challenge — I went back to source rather than just restating the original claim. Three things I checked just now:

1. **The generator's own dedup logic proves a clean run can't produce this.** `scripts/generateRegistry.mjs:979-983` builds a `Set` keyed by component name and filters out any repeat: `if (seen.has(r.name)) return false`. By design, one component name can never appear twice in a real single run — the code is explicitly written to prevent it. Seeing it twice means two separate generator outputs got concatenated (matching a merge conflict resolved by keeping both sides' text instead of regenerating).

2. **It's not just App.** Five more components in the same file are doubled the same way: `ZimmIcon` (10 vs 9 consumers), `ZimmDrawer` (5 vs 5), `ZimmSearchInput` (3 vs 3), `ZimmSubscribeModal` (5 vs 4), `ZimmProductStyleCode` (4 vs 3). Each pair is consistent with two different points in time getting concatenated.

3. **App's case is the worst of the six specifically because it's not just a count mismatch.** The other five at least agree with themselves on origin and file path — only the consumer count is off by one. App's two rows disagree on the classification itself: one says `Override` at `overrides/app/components/_app/index.tsx`, the other says `Base` at `app/components/_app/index.jsx`. Whoever/whatever reads this file next gets a coin-flip answer to "is `_app` overridden" — which is the actual subject of this PR.

That last point is also why it's not just a cosmetic nitpick: `.claude/skills/feature-spec/SKILL.md:39-40` reads `.claude/registry/components.md`/`hooks.md` as its source of truth whenever the folder exists, and only falls back to scanning the codebase directly if it doesn't. It exists, so a future planning session asking "is `_app` already overridden?" would read this file uncritically and could get either answer.

So: both rows having non-null consumer counts is exactly why this is worth flagging rather than obviously broken on a skim — it's not that the data looks garbled, it's that the file is mechanically proven to be two snapshots stitched together, and the App row specifically flips the one fact this PR is about.
